meta.engine: SP/spam/v121/dl/simulation.js (v1.21, model engineHash 36e2c03d5b7bf4a1) + 10 exact-substring patches re-applied on the renamed v1.21 anchors (le, _e, se, be; helpers bound to O, ce, se, T, w, g, o) — make_engine121.js; threats via globalThis.STRESS, default off

validation.note: orig v1.21 vs stress engine, threats off: evaluate(), Z(), per-match loop, STRESS={}, x1.5/x2 damage; named decks also equal check121.json (s1, x1.5, x2) exactly

crosscheckT1.explanation: when we play 2nd (same timing for both methods) 63/72 within ±0.5 and 70/72 within ±5 (2 Scorch outliers: the 1-HP fake card soaks turn-1 damage and flips a death). All large gaps are when we play 1st on Dragon Ciel decks: Dragon Ciel has Vengeur (avenger: its abilities become ready when an ally dies); the fake dead-card dies at the END of turn 1, the cross-check variant fired the on-death trigger at the START of turn 1 (one extra early cast). With the trigger at the enemy action instead, Keria/Dragon Ciel positions agree within 2–8 points; the remaining gaps are cards that act in turn 1 before being absorbed.

deadCardBias.note: dead-card loss-from-turn-1 (check121 L) vs a clean removal at the start of turn 1 (no on-death trigger), 18 named decks: Dragon Ciel decks (non-Dragon card removed) get +540 points on average (play 1st +394, 2nd +687, max +1,701) because the fake card dies in turn 1 and triggers Dragon Ciel Vengeur (its abilities become ready); other decks +18 (the 50-Spamton bounty). check121 L therefore overstates Dragon Ciel decks.

readings.net: J with offense counted net of the HP the enemy gained that turn (absorb gain, heal, revive), same turn weights, floored at 0 per match; equals engine for CDR, SET, DPS and won matches

meta.worst: min over the 5 realistic threats (ABS_nat, CDR_nat, SUS_h32, SUS_rev, SET_nat; net reading; each clamped at base — a threat cannot help a real player)
meta.meanDrop: mean % drop over the same 5 realistic threats
meta.tgt: card number at the worst position (net reading) for positional scenarios

scenarios.ABS_nat: Veuve noire (Tisseuse de Mots #123, absorbAny, CD 8) at its natural turn (7 if we play 1st, 8 if 2nd) on our worst position: the card leaves play, the living enemy with most HP gains its max HP
scenarios.CDR_nat: Rayonnement (Gardien Vert #78, CD 5) resets ONE target card's cooldowns to full at turns 4+9 (we 1st) / 5+10 (we 2nd), worst target
scenarios.SUS_h32: enemy heals 32 HP per turn (median healer card of the data), split over its damaged living cards
scenarios.SUS_rev: the first enemy card killed revives once at 50 % of its max HP (Phénix R / Résurrection)
scenarios.SET_nat: Corne 25 (Cornu mythologique #139, CD 7) sets one of our cards to 25 % of max HP at turn 6 (we 1st) / 7 (we 2nd), worst target
scenarios.ABS_T4: Veuve noire forced at turn 4, worst position
scenarios.ABS_T6: Veuve noire forced at turn 6, worst position
scenarios.ABS_T8: Veuve noire forced at turn 8, worst position
scenarios.DPS_x1.5: abstract opponent damage o.opponent.dpsByTurn x1.5 (no other threat)
scenarios.DPS_x2: abstract opponent damage o.opponent.dpsByTurn x2 (no other threat)
